cards.title: Experimental Unit Definition and Pseudoreplication
cards.claim: The experimental unit is the smallest biological entity independently assigned to a treatment group. Treating technical replicates (e.g., multiple cells from one mouse) or sub-samples as independent units constitutes pseudoreplication, artificially inflating sample size and invalidating statistical inference.
conditions: Applicable when analyzing data with hierarchical structures (e.g., cells within animals, samples within cages).
Requires clear identification of the unit of randomization.
Applies to both destructive and longitudinal sampling designs.
required_inputs: Explicit definition of the experimental unit for each experiment.
Mapping of each observation to its specific experimental unit ID.
Information on whether units were independently randomized or nested.
limitations: Does not define the statistical model itself, only the unit of analysis.
Cannot resolve ambiguity if the original study design did not specify the unit of randomization.
Abstract-only sources may not provide sufficient detail to distinguish unit types.
cards.downstream_use: Determines the correct denominator for n in statistical tests and guides the selection of mixed-effects models versus simple t-tests/ANOVA.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Destructive samples, pooled specimens, biological and technical replicates: independent experimental units and descriptive uncertainty

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
